title: Epp solutions for essentially finite type traits, stable under further extension
statement:
Let $D$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $T$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $H$ and an injective local homomorphism $D\to T$, inducing $F\subseteq H$. Local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal. Suppose that $T$ is essentially of finite type over $D$: there exist a finitely generated commutative $D$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ such that $T\cong A_{\mathfrak p}$ as $D$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then there exists a finite field extension $F_1/F$ [def-pc-field-extension] with the following property for every further finite extension $M/F_1$. Let $R_M\subseteq M$ be the integral closure of $D$ in $M$, and let $B_M$ be the integral closure of the image of $T$ in $(H\otimes_F M)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the subscript means quotienting by all nilpotent elements. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B_M$, set $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak q\cap R_M$. Then $\mathfrak n$ is maximal, $(B_M)_{\mathfrak q}$ is a discrete valuation ring, and
\[
\mathfrak n(B_M)_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q(B_M)_{\mathfrak q}.
\]
Moreover, writing $k_M=R_M/\mathfrak n$ and $k_{\mathfrak q}=(B_M)_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q(B_M)_{\mathfrak q}$, the algebra $k_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{k_M}\Omega$ is reduced for every field extension $\Omega/k_M$. Here reduced means having no nonzero nilpotent element. Neither the characteristic, perfectness of the residue field of $D$, nor separability of $F_1/F$ or $M/F_1$ is restricted.

proof.text: Call a finite extension a strong solution when all normalized local pairs have maximal-ideal equality and separable residue extension. We use separable in the possibly transcendental sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. For any algebraic $P/F$ for which the lower normalization is Noetherian, [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], case (b), gives finitely many upper branches, local DVRs, maximal contractions and finitely generated residue extensions. Its hypothesis holds because the given presentation $T\cong A_{\mathfrak p}$ is exactly essential finite type; no finite type hypothesis on the whole ring $T$ is being substituted.

If the residue characteristic of $D$ is zero, apply [lem-sfb-epp-weak-perfect-residue] to $D\to T$; finite generation of its residue extension follows from Step 1 with $P=F$. This gives a weak solution $N/F$. By case (a) of [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], every lower residue field after this finite extension is finite over the characteristic-zero residue field of $D$, hence still has characteristic zero. Every upper residue field is finitely generated over its lower one by case (b). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis] to obtain a separating transcendence basis for each such extension. These extensions are separable by [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-separable]. Thus $N$ is a strong solution. In positive residue characteristic continue with Steps 3–5; in characteristic zero skip to Step 6 with $F_1=N$.

Suppose the residue characteristic is $p>0$. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-perfect-residue-algebraic-tower] to obtain $P/F$ with lower normalization $D'$ a DVR and perfect residue field $k'$. Step 1 gives the upper normalization $T'$ of $T$ in $(H\otimes_FP)_{\mathrm{red}}$, its finitely many maximal ideals $q_1,\ldots,q_s$, local DVRs $V_a=T'_{q_a}$, and finitely generated residue extensions $\kappa(q_a)/k'$. Apply [lem-sfb-epp-weak-perfect-residue] separately to each local map $D'\to V_a$ to obtain finite extensions $N_a/P$. No essential finite type over $D'$ is needed by this input. Each weak solution is strong: the finite lower residue extensions are perfect by [lem-per-algebraic-extension-perfect], the upper residues remain finitely generated by the finite residue assertions of [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], and [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis] and [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-separable] give separability.

source.place: Tag 09II, p-base preparation and paragraph applying Epp to the localizations of B'

proof.text: Put all the finitely many $N_a$ in a common extension field, using [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] repeatedly, and replace that field by their compositum $P_1$. This is finite over $P$: at each binary compositum [lem-weil-pbc-compositum-degree-bound] gives finite degree over the preceding field, and products of finite spanning sets span the composite over $P$. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-index-one-separable-base-change] to every local pair in the normalization over $N_a$, with the finite further base extension to the corresponding field factor over $P_1$. The local identifications needed here are: $(E\otimes_FN)_{\mathrm{red}}\otimes_NM$ and $E\otimes_FM$ have the same reduction (a nilpotent stays nilpotent after tensoring); integral closure through an intermediate integral ring is unchanged by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive]; and localizing that closure gives the local integral closure by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization]. Consequently all normalized local pairs above every $V_a$ over $P_1$ have maximal-ideal equality and separable residue extension.

source.place: Tag 09II, common solution paragraph; Tags 09EQ and 0GLR; Tag 0307

proof.text: Let $R_\infty$ and $C_\infty$ be the lower and upper normalizations for $P_1/F$. Transitivity of integrality identifies $R_\infty$ with the integral closure of $D'$ in $P_1$. The finite-extension case of [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure] applied to $D'$ makes this ring Noetherian with finitely many maximal ideals. Its algebraic-extension case applied to the original essentially finite type map $D\to T$ then gives the corresponding assertions for $C_\infty$ and finitely generated residue extensions. Localizing at each $q_a$ and using [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] identifies their local pairs with the pairs of Step 4. They therefore satisfy maximal-ideal equality and separability. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-dvr-normalized-finite-stage-descent] hold for $P_1/F$: algebraicity is transitive since $P/F$ is algebraic and $P_1/P$ finite. It supplies a finite subextension $F_1/F$ which is a strong solution.

source.place: Tag 09II, passage to A'_1 and B'_1 and finite-stage descent

proof.text: Let $M/F_1$ be any further finite extension, including an inseparable one. The finite case of [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure] gives the local DVR branches and maximal contractions for both $F_1/F$ and $M/F$. Fix a branch for $M$, and contract it to the branch over $F_1$ (the same structure result gives the contractions). Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-index-one-separable-base-change] to the latter strong local pair and the finite base fraction-field extension determined by $M$. Its normalized local pair is the chosen $M$-branch: use the reduced tensor associativity, transitivity of integrality and localization-of-integral-closure identifications of Step 4, with the same two cited integral-closure lemmas. Thus $\mathfrak n$ is maximal, $(B_M)_{\mathfrak q}$ is a DVR, $\mathfrak n(B_M)_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q(B_M)_{\mathfrak q}$, and $k_{\mathfrak q}/k_M$ is separable. This proves stability by applying the local base-change input, not by assuming stability for weak solutions.

source.place: Tag 0GLR, lemma-solution-goes-up, with omitted details expanded using 09EQ and 0307

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], case (b) for the finite extension $M/F$, the residue extension $k_{\mathfrak q}/k_M$ is finitely generated as a field extension. Separability from Step 6 and clause (2) of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], applied to the whole finitely generated extension itself, make it separably generated. For every field extension $\Omega/k_M$, $\Omega$ is reduced, so [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced] gives that $k_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{k_M}\Omega$ is reduced. This is precisely the final clause, with no perfectness or separability assumption added to $D$, $F_1/F$ or $M/F_1$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q11-c52703959 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all five new nodes, every cited statement and Stacks more-algebra.tex in full: 09II proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type (all of it), 09F9 theorem-epp, 09IH, 0GLR, 09EM, 09EQ, 09E7 and definition-solution. No changes made. The item statement is identical to live, apart from cleaned TeX escapes. The seven steps follow 09II: Step 2 handles residue characteristic 0 by weak Epp plus a perfect residue field. Step 3 builds the p-base perfect-residue tower, applies weak Epp to each branch D'->V_a and makes the weak solutions strong. Step 4 takes a common finite composite and lifts by the index-one base-change node (09EQ via 09E7). Step 5 uses the 09IH structure and finite-stage descent. Step 6 handles every finite M/F_1, including inseparable M, through the index-one node; this is 0GLR with its omitted details written out. Step 7 gives reduced k_q tensor Omega from separably generated plus reduced Omega. Every hypothesis is checked at its step. New nodes are true on tests: the tower node (p-independent stages are DVRs, union has residue field k^perf), weak Epp (for finitely generated kappa_B over a perfect k, the infinitely p-divisible part is algebraic, so Epp's hypothesis holds), the normalization structure node (Krull-Akizuki and 09IH; finitely many maximal ideals; maximal contractions), the index-one node (tested on Z_p with sqrt p, F_p[[t]] with t^{1/p} and a transcendental residue extension, and the identity) and the descent node. The descent node faithfully states the conditional conclusion of the last paragraph of 09II; whoever splits it must expand Stacks' sketchy 'increase i' separability step. No duplicates: the lem-per-epp-* nodes are mixed-characteristic, perfect-residue, excellent-T Gabber IV statements, and the lem-sbc-dvr-* nodes carry tame, root or formally-unramified hypotheses; same_as = []. Accepted tool_uses: separably-generated-separable, common-extension-fields and separably-generated-tensor-reduced, all generic field lemmas. No SGA. Mechanical finding on lem-per-algebraic-extension-perfect: rejected. It is a live mathlib leaf (Algebra.IsAlgebraic.perfectField), listed as dropped only because it became unreached, and another node already cites it. It states only that an algebraic extension of a perfect field is perfect, which is none of the excluded inputs (Qbar_l or adic restatement, Qbar_l duality or biduality, middle t-structure, Gabber finiteness or uniformization, alterations, stable reduction). This item is not lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve or one of its children, and Step 3 justifies the use at a named point. No other node states the fact. Minor wording, no FIX needed: Step 5 does not name the D'->D' pair for case (a), and Step 7 leaves implicit that R_M is Noetherian.
